body:
## Summary

Passport machine-readable zones (ICAO Doc 9303 MRZ) are not detected at all. In a real publication of sanitized AI coding sessions, several MRZ lines of real passports passed through `createSanitizer().sanitize()` unchanged and became public. The data was contained, but passport data is critical personal data and must never pass.

## Reproduction (synthetic data)

```js
import { createSanitizer } from '@link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer';
const s = createSanitizer();
console.log((await s.sanitize(
  'mrz: P<RUSKOVALEVA<<MARINA<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<\n5839204716RUS8204117M310519<<<<<<<<<<<<<<02'
)).text);
// Both lines are returned unchanged, even with the "mrz:" label.
```

## Expected

Detect all ICAO 9303 MRZ formats regardless of context:

- TD3 (passports, 2 x 44 characters), TD2 (2 x 36), TD1 (ID cards, 3 x 30), MRV-A/MRV-B visas.
- The name line (`P<`, `I<`, `A<`, `C<`, `V<` + issuing state + names with `<` fillers).
- The data line, also when only a fragment is present (document number + check digit + nationality + birth date + check digit + sex + expiry + check digit). Real logs often contain a truncated or reflowed line.
- Validate check digits (7-3-1 weights) to raise confidence, but do NOT require valid check digits to redact: a typo in a real MRZ is still personal data.
- New types such as `PASSPORT_MRZ`, category `personal`.

## Tests

- Positive: synthetic TD1/TD2/TD3 lines with valid and invalid check digits; line fragments; MRZ embedded in JSON strings with `\n` escapes; lowercase-free OCR variants with spaces between groups.
- Negative: long runs of `<` alone, base64 strings, C++ templates like `vector<<int>>`.
- Residual verification must fail if an MRZ survives.

Competitors: no open tool has a complete MRZ detector (Presidio only touches TD1 inside the German ID recognizer), so this would be a real differentiator.
title: Detect passport machine-readable zones (ICAO 9303 MRZ): real passport data leaked
